Is this token or link safe?

  • GoPlus Security

    Checks tokens, contracts and links for common scam and honeypot risks.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open the GoPlus website and find its token security checker.
    2. Choose the blockchain network the token lives on, such as Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana or TRON.
    3. Paste the contract address. Copy it from the project's official website or from CoinGecko, not from a chat message, then run the check.
    4. Read the warnings first: honeypot (you can buy but not sell), very high buy or sell tax, an owner who can mint new tokens or change the rules, and hidden owners.
    5. If the report shows several risks, do not buy or approve anything. If it looks clean, remember that is only one input.

    A clean scan is not a guarantee. New scams are built to pass checks, and the tool cannot see the team's plans.

    Level: Beginner
    Open GoPlus Security (opens in a new tab)

What is it worth right now?

  • DefiLlama

    DeFi protocol rankings, TVL and chain data in one place.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open DefiLlama and look at the DeFi rankings by TVL (total value locked).
    2. Click a project and check how its TVL changed over time and on which blockchains it runs.
    3. Watch for sudden drops, or TVL that is mostly the project's own token. That can look bigger than it is.
    4. Look for audit and past hack information on the page, and check the stablecoin and chain pages for context.
    5. Treat very high yields with suspicion. High yield usually means high risk.

    TVL measures how much is deposited. It does not measure how safe a project is.

    Level: Beginner
    Open DefiLlama (opens in a new tab)

  • CoinGecko

    Prices, market caps and basic data for thousands of coins.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open the CoinGecko website and type the token's name or ticker in the search box.
    2. Pick the result with the right name and symbol. Fake tokens copy names, so compare the contract address on the page with the one the project publishes on its own website.
    3. Look at market cap, 24-hour trading volume and the number of markets. Very low volume, or one tiny market, means a single trade can move the price.
    4. Use the official website and social links listed on the token page, not links sent to you in a chat.
    5. Open the price chart with the longest range to see the whole history, and check which exchanges list the token.

    CoinGecko shows data. It does not tell you whether a token is safe or will rise.

    Level: Beginner
    Open CoinGecko (opens in a new tab)

  • TradingView

    Interactive price charts, indicators and community ideas.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open TradingView and search for a coin or trading pair.
    2. Choose a time frame. Start with the daily chart, which is calmer than minute charts.
    3. Add at most one or two indicators, such as volume and a moving average. More does not mean clearer.
    4. Read community ideas as opinions only. Check who wrote them and whether they were right before.
    5. Practise with the paper trading mode, which uses no real money, and check the limits of the free plan.

    Charts show the past. Ideas from other people are not advice.

    Level: Beginner
    Open TradingView (opens in a new tab)

What is this project really about?

  • Token Metrics

    AI-driven token ratings and market research reports.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Token Metrics and search for the token you want to look at.
    2. Read what the rating is made of, not only the headline number. Open the details behind each part.
    3. Compare it with two other sources, such as CoinGecko for market data and the project's own documents.
    4. Check the date of every report. Markets change fast and an old rating can be out of date.
    5. Before paying, check which features need a paid plan and what the free version includes.

    An AI rating is a model's opinion. It is not a prediction and not advice.

    Level: Beginner
    Open Token Metrics (opens in a new tab)

  • Messari

    Research reports, protocol data and an AI assistant for digging into projects.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Messari and search for the project by name.
    2. Read the project profile and research: what it does, who is behind it, how it makes money and what the risks are.
    3. Use the AI assistant for specific questions, then open the source links it gives and check them.
    4. Check the date of the data and which parts are free and which need a paid plan.
    5. Write down three lines in your own words: what it does, how it earns, and the main risk. If you cannot, you do not understand it yet.

    Reports describe projects. They do not tell you when to buy or sell.

    Level: Intermediate
    Open Messari (opens in a new tab)

What is everyone saying?

  • Kaito

    AI search across crypto news, social posts and research to track narratives.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Kaito and type a project or topic in plain words.
    2. Read the sources behind each answer. Open the original posts and articles, not only the summary.
    3. Look for topics that repeat over several days. A narrative is not one loud post.
    4. Check who is posting. Paid promotion and bot accounts can make attention look bigger than it is.
    5. Confirm any claim on the project's official website or on CoinGecko before you act on it.

    Attention is not value. A token that everyone talks about can still be a scam.

    Level: Intermediate
    Open Kaito (opens in a new tab)

  • Santiment

    Social sentiment and on-chain metrics to see what the crowd is talking about.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Santiment and search for an asset.
    2. Look at social volume and sentiment next to the price over weeks, not hours.
    3. Note sudden spikes in talk and ask whether they came before or after a price move.
    4. Add one on-chain metric, such as active addresses, to see if real usage matches the talk.
    5. Check which metrics need a paid plan and whether the free data is delayed.

    Crowd mood is noisy and can be manipulated. It is not a signal to trade.

    Level: Intermediate
    Open Santiment (opens in a new tab)

What are big wallets doing?

  • Nansen

    On-chain analytics with labelled wallets to follow what large players do.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Nansen and start from a token page or a wallet address.
    2. Find the labelled wallets, such as exchanges and funds, and see what they hold.
    3. Check whether a big move is one wallet shifting funds between its own addresses or a real sale.
    4. Compare flows to and from exchanges with the price over the same period.
    5. This is an advanced, mostly paid tool. Look at what the free version shows before you pay.

    Labels are estimates and can be wrong. Following large wallets does not guarantee gains.

    Level: Advanced
    Open Nansen (opens in a new tab)

  • Arkham Intelligence

    Wallet and entity tracking across blockchains with visual explorers.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Arkham and paste a wallet address or search for a name.
    2. Open the visual explorer to see which addresses and entities the wallet deals with.
    3. Read the labels carefully. An address with no label is unknown, not safe.
    4. Follow the largest transfers and see where the money went, for example an exchange or a new wallet.
    5. If alerts are available, set one for an address you want to watch.

    Linking an address to a real person or company can be wrong. Do not accuse anyone based on a label.

    Level: Intermediate
    Open Arkham Intelligence (opens in a new tab)

  • Glassnode

    Deep on-chain metrics and market-cycle indicators, mainly Bitcoin and Ethereum.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Glassnode and start with the free dashboards for Bitcoin and Ethereum.
    2. Learn one metric at a time. Read its description first, for example active addresses or supply held by long-term holders.
    3. Look at long periods, such as several years, not only the last few days.
    4. Compare the metric with the price in earlier cycles to see how it behaved before.
    5. Check which metrics are paid before you subscribe. Most advanced ones are.

    On-chain metrics describe the past. They do not predict what comes next.

    Level: Advanced
    Open Glassnode (opens in a new tab)

  • Dune

    Community dashboards and SQL queries on public blockchain data.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open Dune and search for a dashboard by project name.
    2. Open a community dashboard and read its title, author and last update date.
    3. Check which blockchain it covers and what exactly it counts. Definitions differ between dashboards.
    4. Compare two dashboards for the same project. If the numbers differ, find out why.
    5. Only if you know SQL: copy a query to your own account and change one thing at a time.

    Anyone can publish a dashboard. Check the author and the data before you trust a chart.

    Level: Advanced
    Open Dune (opens in a new tab)

Before you use any crypto tool

  • Never share your seed phrase or private keys. No real tool, support agent or admin will ask for them.
  • Nobody can promise a profit. Be careful with anyone who does, even in a friendly chat.
  • Open tools by typing the address yourself or from this list. Fake sites copy real ones.
  • Try a free plan first, and check the price on the official site before you pay.
